Quests: lv2_orchard_thieves (Hana Pipp), lv2_singing_roots (Nell; reveals the Root Hollows), lv2_lantern_oil (Tobben; Duskmane scouts). Generated by Tools/datagen/lv2/gen_lv2.py.

creatures.name: Wandering Rootling
creatures.description: A little rootling up from under Old Kusu, with an apple under each arm and a guilty look.
creatures.bark: *The rootling clutches its apple and creaks defensively.*

creatures.name: Rootling Sapling
creatures.description: A rootling with a glowing bud. It patches up its friends with sap, and its friends patch up the apples.

creatures.name: Duskmane Scout
creatures.description: A gnoll of the Duskmane clan, a long way east of Amberfield. Lean, nervous and smelling powerfully of lamp oil.
creatures.bark: *The gnoll's ears go flat and it shows a great many teeth.*

creatures.name: Duskmane Lookout
creatures.description: A gnoll archer with a green bandana and a bow it is very proud of.

creatures.name: Wheatfield Tusker
creatures.description: A boar that has discovered Ama Hollyhock's wheat and is not prepared to un-discover it.

creatures.name: Old Bristlesow
creatures.description: The tuskers' mother: broad as a cart, grizzled, and absolutely certain the wheat is hers.
creatures.bark: *Old Bristlesow snorts, lowers her tusks and scrapes the furrow with one hoof.*

abilities.name: Barbed Arrow

npcs.name: Hana Pipp
npcs.title: <Orchard-keeper>
npcs.bark: One bite. ONE bite. Out of every single apple!

npcs.name: Ama Hollyhock
npcs.title: <Beekeeper>
npcs.bark: Mind the bees, dear. They don't mind you.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Look — the rootling row! I leave them the windfalls and a lantern on the fence, and they chase the wasps off and sing to the blossom. Best harvest in ten years. Don't tell the other orchards.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Sprout? He sleeps in the crate you found, under a sack. He's taken one bite out of my hat. I'm choosing to find it charming.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Not one bitten apple since. I've started counting them again for fun. Four thousand and twelve. Four thousand and eleven — I just ate one.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Well? Did you catch them? Who's been eating my apples?

choices.text: Rootlings — little sprouts of Old Kusu, up from under the roots. They were lost and hungry, not wicked.
Some root-creatures. They won't trouble you again.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Sprouts of Old Kusu? Walking about? *She looks at the bitten apples in a new light.* ...Well, they've got the manners of saplings. What do I do — chase them off with a broom every night?

choices.text: They come up looking for light. Leave them the windfalls and a lantern, and they'll guard your trees from worse things.
The earth spirits ask you to share with them. They'll pay you back in blossom.
Every lantern is for everyone, Hana. Even the little wooden ones.
Keep your crates covered, and they'll find somewhere else.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Guard my trees? Those little thieves? *She narrows her eyes at you, then at the orchard.* I'll keep the crates covered, thank you.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: A row for the rootlings... *She laughs.* My granny used to leave a bowl out for 'the little folk'. I thought she meant hedgehogs. All right. One row, one lantern, all the windfalls they can carry.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Gone, then. Good. *She sounds relieved, and a tiny bit sorry.* Here — for your trouble, and a bag of the ones they didn't get to.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: And take your pick from the shed. Grandad's things — he'd want them used, not dusted.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: The crate's in the middle of the orchard, by the third row. Look for the apples with one bite out. They are all of them.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Mind the windfalls! Hana Pipp — the orchard's mine. Well. Mine, the bees', and lately SOMEBODY ELSE'S.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Forty-eight trees, planted by my great-great-grandad the year the village got its first lantern. Old Kusu's roots run right under them — that's why the apples taste of honey. Everybody says so. I say so loudest.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Every night something gets in and takes ONE bite out of every apple. One! It isn't even greedy, it's just rude. They had a party round the crate in the middle row last night — have a look, would you? I'd go, but I'd lose my temper, and then my broom.

nodes.speaker: lv2_hana_pipp
nodes.text: Bless you. If it's the Fernsby children, bring them back by the ear. If it's anything else, use your judgement. I trust your judgement. I don't trust the Fernsby children.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The apple crate lies on its side. Every apple has exactly one neat bite out of it, and the soft earth around it is stippled with tiny prints — not paws, not boots. More like the ends of roots.

choices.text: Take a closer look at those 'footprints'.
Wait among the trees and see who comes back for seconds.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The prints wander from tree to tree, one bite per apple, and they are fresh: a few minutes old. Whoever it is, they're still in the north rows.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The prints go round the crate, round the next tree, round you... You stop before you get dizzy.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Those aren't feet — they're root-tips, the kind a sapling puts down. Something rooty has walked up here from under Old Kusu. It has also, clearly, been enjoying itself.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Squirrels, you decide firmly. Very heavy squirrels. With roots.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A rustle in the north rows. Something small, pale and root-legged trundles between the trees with an apple in its arms — and it is not alone.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A tipped apple crate. Every apple in it has one neat bite out of it. Somebody has very good manners, or very small mouths.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The great root is warm under your hand, and the hum is louder now that you know where it comes from: the mossy mouth between the two biggest roots, breathing cool air up from below.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You kneel and press your ear to the great root. It is warm. Under the bark something hums — one long, low note, wavering like a voice trying very hard not to cry.

choices.text: Listen for where the note comes from.
Read the root itself: the bark, the sap, the way it runs.
Say a quiet prayer with the old tree.
Ask the spirits of the earth what is wrong.
Feel for the draught on your face, the way you would in a fox's earth.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The note isn't in the root at all. It's coming up through it, from below — from the mound of moss and fern between the two biggest roots, where a cool draught is breathing out of the ground. There is a hollow under Old Kusu. And something in it is singing.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You listen until your ear goes numb. The note goes on and on, from everywhere and nowhere at once.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The sap is running the wrong way: down, not up, drawn towards the mound of moss between the two biggest roots as if something under it is drinking. When you push the ferns aside, cold air breathes out of a dark mouth in the earth.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It's a root. A very big, very old, very warm root. Beyond that, the tree keeps its own counsel.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: In the quiet of the prayer the note becomes a word, or nearly: 'below'. When you open your eyes, the ferns on the mossy mound between the roots are stirring in a breeze that is coming out of the ground.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The tree is old and patient and not, at the moment, talking to you.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The earth answers slowly, the way old earth does: the roots are hurting, because the one who guards them is hurting. He is below. The way down is under the moss between the two biggest roots.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: There — on your cheek, from the left. Cool air, steady as breath, coming out of the mound of moss and fern between the two biggest roots. Something below has a way in, and a way out.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You listen. The note rises a little, as if it is glad someone has noticed, then sinks back into the dark under the tree.

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *Three gnolls look up from Tobben's oil casks: two with notched cleavers, one with a bow and a very guilty expression.* Hrrk. Not yours. Found it. Finders-keepers is gnoll law, yes?

choices.text: Those casks belong to Lanternvale. Put them down.
Drop the oil and run, or I'll make a rug out of you.
Gnolls don't burn lamp oil. What do you want it for?
Toss them the smoked boar haunch from your pack.
Point past them and gasp: 'Is that a BEAR?'

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *The scout bares every one of its teeth.* Then come take, small lantern-person!

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *The gnolls cackle — a little too loudly.* Big words! Small lantern-person! Get them!

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *All three gnolls look at you, then at each other, then at the horizon.* ...Rug. No. Not rug. Keep oil. Bad oil. Smelly. *They are gone in a scrabble of claws and a cloud of dust.*

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *The haunch sails over their heads. Three noses follow it. Three gnolls follow their noses. Somewhere over the hill, a fight breaks out over who gets the bone.*

choices.text: (Roll the casks back to the road.)

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *Three heads whip round. By the time they turn back, you are sitting on the oil casks, filing your nails. The gnolls decide, as one, that this is witchcraft, and leave.*

choices.text: (Roll the casks back to the road.)

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *The scout squints at you.* Why lantern-person ask so many why? Suspicious. VERY suspicious.

choices.text: Those casks belong to Lanternvale. Put them down.

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *The scout's ears droop.* ...Lights in the west going grey. Grey comes in the night, and in the morning the old ones don't wake. Big Chief says fire keeps the grey away. Oil makes fire. We take oil, we stay warm. Yes?

choices.text: Take one cask and go home. The other two stay — the valley needs them for Walk Night.

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *Long pause. Much ear-twitching.* ...One. Fair. One for Duskmane, two for lantern-people. *The smallest gnoll hugs its cask like a puppy.* You tell Big Chief, Snaggle was fair. Snaggle was VERY fair.

nodes.speaker: lv2_snaggle
nodes.text: *The scout looks at the three casks, then at you, then at the three casks.* No. Three is more than one. Gnoll maths.

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: *An old man in a battered hat doesn't take his eyes off his float.* Evening. Or morning. Whichever it is, keep your shadow off the water. The big one's listening.

choices.text: Have you heard the roots behind Old Kusu?

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: Three boots, a kettle and Bram's hat. The hat was still on Bram. Long story.

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: Old Grandfather Carp. Older than me, longer than me, and cleverer than me by a whisker. Forty years I've been trying. I think he comes up to laugh.

choices.text: Let me help you land him.

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: *You take the line just as it goes taut. For one glorious moment a golden back the size of a door breaks the water — then the line goes slack, and a single huge scale floats to the surface.* ...He let us see him. Forty years. Ha! HA! Here — take this, for luck.

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: *The line twangs, you sit down very suddenly in the reeds, and something under the water makes a noise exactly like a laugh.* See? Every time.

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: Hear them? Ha. I've lit lanterns forty years, and the old lamplighters told me: Kusu's roots carry the light, same as a wick carries oil. When they hum, all's well. Lately they don't hum. They moan. The frogs go quiet when they start.

choices.text: Is there a way down to the roots?

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: There used to be a Root Lantern, down under the tree, that the first lamplighters tended. Nobody's been down in my lifetime. If there's a door, it's grown over. You'd want sharp ears to find it — or a child's. Children always know where the doors are.

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: Forty years, man and boy. I lit the Walk Night lanterns the year the Warden came down so close I could have touched his antlers. I didn't. You don't. Now Tobben does the ladders and I do the fish.

nodes.speaker: lv2_teo
nodes.text: Anything else? Quietly, mind.

choices.text: Have you heard the roots behind Old Kusu?

nodes.speaker: lv2_ama_hollyhock
nodes.text: Mind the bees, dear — they don't mind you. Ama Hollyhock. That's my farm, my wheat, my bees, and that scarecrow is my late husband's coat, so be respectful.

nodes.speaker: lv2_ama_hollyhock
nodes.text: You've a good eye. They don't like the north wind this year. It smells of smoke, they say, though there's no fire anywhere. Bees know things. I just sell the honey.

nodes.speaker: lv2_ama_hollyhock
nodes.text: Restless? Dear, they're bees. They've been restless since the beginning of the world.

nodes.speaker: lv2_ama_hollyhock
nodes.text: Boars! Old Bristlesow and her great lumps of sons. They've flattened a quarter of the east field already. If you were to... discourage them, I'd bake you something. I bake very well.

nodes.speaker: lv2_ama_hollyhock
nodes.text: Born in that very farmhouse. My sister married over the downs in Amberfield — the Haybrights. Her granddaughter Bruna swings a billhook like she's personally offended by hedges. Lovely girl. Frightens the gnolls.

nodes.speaker: lv2_ama_hollyhock
nodes.text: Anything else, dear? The honey won't jar itself.

nodes.speaker: lv2_sprout
nodes.text: *The little rootling holds up an apple with one neat bite out of it and offers it to you, very solemnly.*

quests.name: Bitten, Every One
quests.summary: Something creeps into the Pipp orchard at night and takes exactly one bite out of every apple. Hana Pipp would very much like to know what — and then to have a word with it.

stages.description: Look over the tipped apple crate in the middle of the Pipp orchard, north of the meadow.
Catch the orchard thieves in the north rows.
Tell Hana Pipp who has been eating her apples.

quests.name: The Singing Roots
quests.summary: Moppet says the roots behind Old Kusu are singing. Not happy singing — the kind you do when something hurts and you don't want anyone to know. Grown-ups can't hear it. Nell thinks you might.

stages.description: Listen at the great root behind Old Kusu, north of the village square.
Tell Nell what the roots are singing about.

quests.name: Oil for Walk Night
quests.summary: Three casks of lamp oil have vanished from Tobben's store on the west road, the week before Walk Night. Every lantern in the valley wants filling, and Tobben refuses to light them with good intentions.

stages.description: Look for the casks' trail on the west road, north-west of Old Kusu.

objectives.text: Find the trail on the west road

stages.description: Get the oil back from whoever took it. The trail leads to the old waystation north of the road.
Tell Tobben what became of his oil.
